restrictions: SCOPE: one machine and one environment. The Linux Legacy UI was built and run only on Ubuntu 24.04.5 inside WSL2 with WSLg on a Windows 11 laptop (validation/platforms/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64.json), against the XWayland server of WSLg, as x86_64 here (the i686 build is another platform record, linux-i686, and has its own verdict, linux-i686-legacy). Per ADR 0007 the executable is built on the machine that runs it, so no glibc or libstdc++ ceiling is checked and it was not run on any other system: no real or very old distribution, no other X server (Xorg, a native Wayland session), no window manager decorations (the captures show the client area), no other hardware. This verdict does not determine the Linux floor and says nothing about T092 beyond this platform.

NO TEXT SHAPING AND NO BIDIRECTIONAL LAYOUT, by decision (accepted by the owner, see the fallback record xlib-core-font-glyphs): Xft draws the code points one after the other in logical order, left to right. Arabic letters appear in their isolated forms and left to right, Hebrew and Arabic words appear visually reversed, a ZWJ sequence (a family emoji, a flag) is drawn as its separate components, an Indic conjunct is not formed, a combining mark is placed correctly only when its font gives it a zero advance, and the invisible format characters (ZWSP, ZWJ, bidi controls, variation selectors, BOM, soft hyphen) draw nothing. The stored screenshot xlib-xft-mixed-unicode.png shows the reversed Hebrew, the isolated Arabic and the separate family components.

EMPTY BOX FOR A GLYPH NO FONT HAS: a code point that no installed font provides (U+0378 in the mixed string) is drawn as an empty box and the probe line carries 'missing-glyph' in disabled_features; the greeting and the probe record are unchanged. Which code points have a glyph depends on the fonts of this machine (429 fontconfig fonts on 2026-11-14, per the session log of xlib-unicode-manylinux); no other font set was tried and the coverage of the 15 vectors on a machine with fewer fonts is not known.

CORE-FONT PATH ONLY WHEN XFT IS MISSING AT BUILD TIME: if CMake finds no libXft and fontconfig development files (or LOOMORA_XLIB_XFT=OFF, or at run time LOOMORA_XLIB_NO_XFT, or Xft opens no font) the UI draws with the core X11 font 'fixed', a character it cannot draw is a '?' and the probe line carries 'glyph-substitution' (fallback xlib-core-font-glyphs). The x86_64 build of this platform finds Xft and does NOT take it; the fallback was measured on builds without Xft (stored: the i686 build before the 32-bit Xft packages were installed, the x86_64 build with LOOMORA_XLIB_NO_XFT of the dlopen version, the 15 vectors of the first core-font build). Under WSLg the core font 'fixed' is -Misc-Fixed-Medium-R-SemiCondensed--13-120-75-75-C-60-ISO8859-1 and the server lists no ISO 10646 font, so only Latin-1 is drawn on that path. NOT verified: the ISO 10646-1 path (XDrawString16) with a real Unicode core font (it was only forced onto the 8-bit font in a test copy, Latin-1 drawn correctly).

INPUT WAS SYNTHETIC: every typed key of the window runs was an XSendEvent with a remapped spare keycode (tools/trials/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/xlib-driver.c), never a physical keyboard, a real layout, key repeat or focus changes by a person. The Xutf8LookupString path was exercised only in the typing runs of the dlopen build (session log of xlib-unicode-manylinux), with whatever input method XOpenIM opened on this server, and the XLookupString plus key symbol table path without one (4 combinations, same text typed). NOT tested: an input-method server such as ibus or fcitx, dead keys, compose sequences, IME composition; clipboard paste is out of scope of the UI.

THE STORED EVIDENCE IS MOSTLY OF EARLIER BUILDS. Only validation/evidence/linux-build-on-target/ belongs to the current builds (native, Xft linked, ADR 0007): the build facts, two probe lines of the mixed string and one screenshot. The folders linux-legacy-xlib/ (first build: static C++ runtime, core font only, 300,960 bytes) and xlib-unicode-manylinux/ (dlopen of Xft, plus manylinux2010 builds removed by ADR 0007) are history: they show the behaviour that did not change (greeting, 1,000-character limit, 15 vectors, sanitizer cleanliness, startup cost) but are not evidence of executable 4d7c91a4. The real-window checks of the current Xft build (mixed Unicode drawn, typing, 1,000 characters kept, close exits 0) are recorded in the deliverable record; of them only the one screenshot and the probe lines above are stored, so the typing, the 1,000-character limit and the close of the CURRENT build are not backed by a stored file.

RE-RUNS ARE NOT STORED (CLAUDE.md): tools/run_vectors.py 15 of 15 (15 run, 15 passed, 16 skipped, 2 truncated to 1,000 characters) for the x86_64 Xft build, with LOOMORA_XLIB_NO_XFT=1 and for the i686 build; ctest 2 of 2; ASan and UBSan with 0 errors in 5 runs on an adapted copy of tools/trials/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/xlib-ui-harness-cpp.cpp (Xft, core font, forced core font, no input method). Their results are in the text of build-facts.txt and of the deliverable record, not as files. The vectors have no emoji, shaping or bidi expectation beyond the probe line (greeting_matches and the 1,000-character cut): they do not check the picture.

END-OF-LIFE BANNER: this platform is not end of life (kernel 6.18 is not treated as such by loomora_is_eol), so eol_warning_shown is false in every probe line of the current build and the banner of the Linux Legacy UI was shown only by a TEST-ONLY build outside the repository whose uname() returns 2.6.32, on the first core-font build (eol-test-build-probe.json, 05-eol-banner-test-build.png). The banner was not re-run on the Xft build and was never shown on a real end-of-life Linux system (the check of T088 for Linux has no real case here).

TIMINGS ARE SINGLE LINES, NOT A SERIES: the stored probe lines of the current build give display_ms 164 and peak_rss_kb 13680 (Xft) once; the 10-run series of the Xft path (display_ms 20 to 25, peak_rss_kb 9056 to 9256) is from the dlopen build of the history folder. No series was run on the current build, and no number here is a performance claim.

NOT DONE (no record or file shows it): HiDPI or a changed Xft.dpi, themes and high-contrast schemes, a second monitor, a long-running or repeated session, memory over time, and the shipped x86_64 executable of the deliverable record (sha256 4d7c91a4...) being re-measured after the build: the x86_64 file of ~/loomora-build/linux-legacy-x86_64 at the time of writing (79,912 bytes) is a later build whose hash differs from the deliverable record, so no stored number is claimed for it.

notes: Verdict of the Linux Legacy UI (Xlib, C++11, CMake, text drawn with Xft and fontconfig) on linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64, written 2026-11-14 from the records and the stored evidence only; it covers the x86_64 part of T092 for this one platform (T092 and T087 stay open) and the Linux part of the Legacy UI checks, not the Linux floor. STATUS ok_restricted because the greeting 'Bonjour Coucou' / 'Bonjour Marie' and the mixed Unicode input are drawn and kept (greeting_matches true in every stored probe line; 15 of 15 reference vectors in the re-runs), but the restrictions above are real: no shaping or bidi, an empty box for a glyph no font has, the core-font path only without Xft at build time, one machine under WSLg, synthetic key events, no input-method server. DECISION keep: nothing found makes the UI unusable on this platform, and the lack of shaping and bidi is accepted by the owner while the other limits are test coverage gaps, not defects found. FALLBACKS (validation/fallbacks.json): cxx17-nodiscard is taken (the UI and the backend are strict C++11, the deliverable record lists it); xlib-core-font-glyphs is NOT taken by this platform's x86_64 build (its platform_ids is empty on purpose, it is decided per build and written by tools/build.py into the deliverable record of a build without Xft); the gtk4-ui id in the deliverable record is the platform-wide list of fallbacks and concerns the Modern UI, not the Xlib UI. BUILD AND CHECK COMMANDS (inside WSL, Ubuntu 24.04, build directory under $HOME/loomora-build): 'python3 tools/build.py linux legacy [--arch x86_64|i686|all]' (native build, writes the deliverable record); 'python tools/run_vectors.py linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64 legacy [--exe <path>]' (from Windows through the WSL launcher or inside WSL); 'ctest' in the build directory; tools/check_probe.py on a probe line; the window drivers and the sanitizer harness in tools/trials/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/ (xlib-driver.c, xlib-ui-harness-cpp.cpp). The text files of the evidence folders keep their LF line endings (validation/evidence/.gitattributes) because this verdict holds their sha256. The replayable procedure is validation/procedures/linux.md (field 'reproduction', written 2026-11-14 and replayed on the same machine that day). EVIDENCE SORTING: [current build] items are the proof for the executable of the deliverable record; [history] items are earlier builds of the same UI (first static core-font build; dlopen Xft build) kept as they were and superseded by ADR 0007 for anything about the build; they are listed because they hold the only stored runs of the 1,000-character limit, the sanitizer sessions, the 15-vector check and the end-of-life banner. NOT DONE and not claimed: a real old Linux distribution, kernel 2.6, a native 32-bit system, any other X server, distribution or font set, a physical keyboard or an input-method server, shaping or bidirectional text (none by decision), HiDPI, and the end-of-life banner on a real end-of-life system. SPEC 002, THE .loomora PROJECT FILE (2026-11-17). HOST NOTE: the spec 002 runs were made on a host with an Intel Core i7-11800H (16 logical CPUs), not on the MSI GL63 8RD of validation/platforms/windows-11-x64.json (the Windows build, 26300.9974, is the same). DISTRIBUTION NOTE: the Linux runs of spec 002 were made in the WSL2 distribution Ubuntu-26.04 (26.04.1 LTS, g++ 15.2.0, clang++ 23.1.6 for the fuzz run, glibc 2.43, kernel 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2) and NOT in the Ubuntu 24.04 distribution that this record describes; tools/run_vectors.py derived the platform id linux-ubuntu-26.04-x86_64, which has no platform record and no verdict, so the results are written here, on the nearest record, and are not a run on Ubuntu 24.04. FORMAT RESULT (Linux x86_64, g++ 15.2.0, Release, Ninja): loomora_format_selftest passes, ctest 3 of 3 (selftest, format_selftest, loomora_tests); tools/verify.py quick in WSL gives 14 passed, 1 failed (std, the vectors of both Linux UIs, cli validate, corpus, ui project and format-files pass; the failure is 'records', expected before this docs branch is used). loomora_refgen writes the six reference files (basic, empty, escape40, multi, multi-light, one); their SHA-256 are the reference of the golden constants of core/tests/format_selftest.cpp and are identical on every target that ran it (hashes in validation/evidence/adr-0021/linux-ubuntu-26.04-x86_64/hashes.json; the files are stored once, under windows-11-x64/). S-F1 ok with g++ 15.2 -std=c++11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -O2 (zlib 1.3.1 and RapidJSON output identical to Windows clang and MinGW). SC-004 FUZZ RUN of the reader (core/tests/fuzz_run_sc004.md of the main repository; logs under $HOME/loomora-build/fuzz-logs, not committed): 12.6 million inputs (6,000,000 libFuzzer in run 1, 4,200,000 in the mutation loop, 2,400,000 libFuzzer in run 2), clang++ 23.1.6 Release with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (-fno-sanitize-recover=undefined) and leak detection on, 15 processes at once on 16 threads with distinct seeds, libFuzzer -timeout=5 -max_len=262144 with the structure-aware mutator (CRC-32 and manifest SHA-256 repaired); seeds: the 114 files of tools/gen_invalid_corpus.py --skip-truncate plus the loomora_refgen files; wall time 2,746 s for run 1 and 720 s for run 2. Result: no crash, no leak, no undefined behaviour, no out-of-bounds access, no sanitizer report, no input slower than 5 s (slowest 0.26 s); nothing to fix, so no regression file was added. Run on this Linux x86_64 distribution only (not on 32-bit, Windows or any old system). SC-005 MEASUREMENT (core/tests/perf_sc005.md of the main repository, loomora_bench_format, Release, g++ 15, i7-11800H, WSL 16 GB, nothing else running): 5,000 nails and 100,000 steps (321 KB): validate 0.008 to 0.010 s, open including validation 0.008 to 0.009 s, reading every step and nail 0.005 s, peak 11 MB, against the required 1 s (met by a factor of about 100); 500,000 nails and 10,000,000 steps (41 MB): validate 1.0 s (one run 1.5 s), open 1.0 s (one run 2.2 s), read 0.6 s (one run 1.4 s), peak 459 MB (/usr/bin/time -v: 470 MB), opened with 0 errors and 2 warnings and not refused (met); 3 repetitions, the slow runs isolated (host noise); no change to core/src/format was needed. SC-010 (tools/verify.py step 'ui project': tools/run_vectors.py --validate-project and --roundtrip-project against `loomora validate --quiet`, byte for byte and by exit status): the Linux Legacy (Xlib, loomora-xlib) UI of the default build matched in 37 of 37 runs (the 6 loomora_refgen files and the 9 valid-* corpus files validated and round-tripped, one invalid file, one missing path, 3 usage rows); no display used; the log is in the build directory and is not stored. T101 REVIEW of core/src/format (validation/bug-reports/format-review-2026-11-17.md, a review by reading, nothing run under a sanitizer, the Windows 2000 code paths read only): 8 findings, 2 confirmed and fixed (the POSIX file layer blocked on a FIFO with a regression test; a data race on the temporary-file name counter, fixed without a failing-first test, the owner may drop that commit) and 6 deferred for the owner (a symbolic link is replaced on save, calendar validity of time stamps, 32-bit truncation in inflate_some, linear costs on large projects, a .old- file may stay after the Windows 2000 rename-aside, the raw copy of kept entries is not re-verified at save); the fixes were verified with tools/verify.py quick on Linux g++ (with and without them) and on Windows clang (baseline only). NOT DONE and not claimed on this record: any run in the Ubuntu 24.04 distribution, a fuzz run on another architecture, a big-endian system (qemu is not installed: not_tested).
